deviation: **Two-phase report generation for cap-hit draws.** The pilot (128 root draws, 8B) gave 83.6% valid reports against the 95% gate. Diagnosis: vLLM forces `</think>` at the thinking budget by a logits boost, but the model does not switch into report mode — it continues its derivation and spends all 256 report tokens on reasoning, emitting no tag at all (0 of 17 truncated draws contained even an opening `<final>`). A prompt-wording repair was tried first and **failed**, moving validity by under one point, because a model mid-derivation does not attend to the instruction. The remedy is the contingency the plan already documented: when and only when phase 1 hits the thinking cap, the report is generated as a `/v1/completions` continuation from the exact phase-1 token prefix through `</think>`, with the `<final>` opening prefilled so the answer comes first. The trigger is `boundary_injected` alone — uniform over every cap-hit draw, never conditioned on what phase 1 produced. Both physical requests are recorded and their FLOPs summed.
spec_clause: §6.2 line 232 (the split budget uses the existing tested backend mechanism; "Preserve exact token IDs across the continuation"; "Count both physical requests and any repeated prefill in runtime cost"), §6.3 lines 250-252
unsupported_claim: This is the more faithful reading of §6.2's *independent* 256-token final allowance: under a forced boundary the genuinely independent report is the continuation, not the tail of an interrupted reasoning stream. The allowances stay 1,024 + 256 and the cap-hit rate remains a reported outcome. What it does limit: a cap-hit report is written from a prefilled opening tag, so its *format* is induced rather than spontaneous, and report-format compliance must not be reported as a model property for those draws.

deviation: **A report span cut by `max_tokens` after `</final>` closed still delivers its answer** (new `ParseStatus.TRUNCATED_AFTER_FINAL`, admitted to `VALID_PARSE_STATUSES`). The parser previously ranked the `truncated` status *above* the `<final>` checks, so any cut span was invalid even when a well-formed `<final>...</final>` had closed before the cut. Spec §6.3 conditions validity on the `<final>` tag alone ("missing/malformed `<final>` = invalid"), so the implementation was stricter than the contract it implements. Found by the two-phase pilot (128 root draws, 8B, train-split items only, pre-freeze): the continuation writes the answer immediately from the prefilled tag (`8</final>`, `0.0996</final>`) and then keeps reasoning inside `<evidence>`, exhausting the 256-token report allowance without closing it. All 16 such draws had committed a closed, non-empty answer. Measured effect on that pilot: validity 0.875 -> 1.000 with 0 of 67 cap-hit draws left undelivered.
spec_clause: §6.3 lines 250-252 (the report schema and its validity rule)
unsupported_claim: The answer channel is unaffected -- these reports commit before the cut. What it does limit is the *confidence* axis: a cut tail loses `<confidence>` (and `<evidence>`), so these draws carry a missing confidence under the frozen missing-is-missing policy, never an imputed 0.5. That missingness is **not random** -- it lands only on cap-hit draws, i.e. the longer, harder items -- so every calibration and confidence panel reports `conf_missing_rate` beside its estimate, the matched-n rule (plan §5.8) governs any cross-round or cross-protocol comparison, and confidence-conditioned controller features carry their existing missing-indicator. On this pilot that is 12.5% of decisions. Report-format compliance is already excluded as a model property for cap-hit draws under I6.

deviation: **The full core tier is restored; the prospective §16.4 downscope is lifted.** The plan applied §16.4 steps 1-3 prospectively at T0 because the clock started with implementation inside the 36 hours (no HUB5, E2d 16 items, challenge <=48, receiver 32, selector audit on two pools, extensions off), reducing the core to 47,424 8B + 8,256 32B decisions. The plan's own condition for restoring the full 62,224 + 9,376 core was that the *measured* projection with the 20% reserve completes by hour 30. At hour 9.7 the launch gate passes all 20 checks on that measured projection: critical path 13.8 h against a 16 h deadline, total 21.6 h against 34 h, and the bundle's own budget_check -- run out of the shipped zip, not paraphrased -- projects 5.36 h for the small lane and 4.29 h for the large lane. The measured rates behind it are 548 tok/s per 8B replica and 342 per 32B replica under real load (7.16 and 1.67 logical decisions/s), measured after defect D-03 raised per-cell concurrency from 1 to N_AGENTS.
unsupported_claim: None to any estimand: the restoration adds arms and items, it removes none, and every reduced-tier cell is a subset of the full-tier manifest. The decision was taken on throughput, validity and replica census alone -- **no test outcome, correctness result or protocol contrast had been computed when it was made**, which is the condition the plan attaches to any tier change. HUB5 re-enters the tier, so its throughput was piloted before the gate rather than assumed. What it does commit: the run now owes the full cohort, so a later shortfall must be reported as incomplete coverage against the full ledger rather than silently rebased.
